title: Operational Fault Lens and Code Alignment Dashboard
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Create a consolidated operational view (Fault Lens) that aligns runtime failure signals across traces, logs, and metrics to canonical error codes and a concise failure taxonomy. The goal is to make it easy for oncall and SREs to: 1) see the predominant root-cause class (timeout, overload, model_error, rejection, transport errors), 2) inspect representative traces with enriched span tags, and 3) map SLI/SLO exposure per route/model. This ticket covers design decisions, enrichment pipeline, dashboard panels, and rollout plan for the Fault Lens.
background: We currently have multiple dashboards for latency islands and error taxonomies but no single pane that ties HTTP/gRPC status codes, model-level errors (e.g., sampling OOM/rejection/model-internal exceptions), and service-level overload signals into one operational workflow. This causes longer incident TTR because engineers must jump between traces, metrics, and ad-hoc logs to correlate a user-facing 5xx with an underlying model rejection or GPU OOM.
goals: 1) Define a deterministic mapping from telemetry to canonical failure classes. 2) Implement tracehook enrichment so spans carry 'fault.class' and 'fault.reason' attributes. 3) Build a Grafana dashboard with: top failure classes by traffic, representative span sampler, per-route SLO exposure, and a Sankey linking transport codes -> fault.class -> impacted models. 4) Add runbook links and one-click sample export for debugging teams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dashboard exposes top 10 fault classes with time-series and heatmap views.
- Each fault class links to a sampled trace set (0.1% baseline, up to 1% during alerts).
- Enrichment attaches attributes: fault.class, fault.subclass, rpc.code/http.status, model.error_code, runtime.node_id.
- Mapping doc published in Confluence and approved by Observability PM.
- Runbook entries added for timeout, overload, model_error, and rejection classes.
- Metrics for SLI exposure per-route added and surfaced on the dashboard.
technical_notes: Telemetry sources: trace spans (OpenTelemetry), metrics (Prometheus), logs (structured JSON to Elastic). Enrichment will run in the trace-ingest path (tracehook) to add 'fault.class' using a deterministic rule engine: priority order: model.error_code -> grpc.status -> http.status -> latency+concurrency heuristics -> rate-limit. Sampling policy: default sample key is service:route:failure_class with probabilistic backfill. Will reuse existing tracehook adapter in /pkg/tracehook and extend it to consult the 'model-runtime-status' span attribute emitted by the runtime. Use pre-aggregation in ClickHouse for heatmaps (route x failure_class) and Grafana for Sankey (via plugin + precomputed edges endpoint).
failure_class_mapping: timeout: spans with model.runtime_exit == 'deadline_exceeded' or grpc.code == 'DEADLINE_EXCEEDED' or http.status == '504'
overload: detected when node.cpu_utilization > 90% OR queue_length > threshold OR grpc.code == 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED' or http.status == '429'
model_error: model-runtime exceptions (batch OOM, nan-loss, decode_error) surfaced as model.error_code != null
rejection: scheduler rejection due to admission control or rate-limit (internal reject event + grpc.code == 'UNAVAILABLE' sometimes), reservation failures
transport_error: network or proxy level 5xx (502/503) where model-runtime did not report an error
client_error: 4xx where upstream input validation or authorization failed (http.status 400-499)
dashboard_panels: Panel: Fault Class Time Series - stacked area of failure classes by token volume and request count
Panel: Route x Fault Heatmap - ClickHouse preagg table: (route, failure_class) -> error_rate over sliding window
Panel: Sankey (transport code -> failure_class -> model) - precomputed edges endpoint /api/ops/fault-edges
Panel: Representative Trace Sampler - list of spans with quick open in Trace UI (link to trace.id)
Panel: SLI Exposure - percent of requests failing SLI grouped by route/model and total request volume impacted
Panel: Oncall Checklist & Runbook Links - quick playbook steps per class
data_pipelines: Tracehook enrichment change: add fault.class,fault.subclass,model.error_code to span attributes (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/tracehook/pull/412)
Metrics ETL: ClickHouse aggregation job (cron hourly) to compute route-failure heatmaps (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability-scripts/pull/289)
Logs: add parser rules in Logstash/Fluentd to forward model runtime errors as structured fields
Edge service: new /api/ops/fault-edges endpoint returns precomputed sankey edges (backend PR pending)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misclassification (e.g., marking transport 5xx as model_error) -> mitigate by conservative rules and a 'suspect' subclass for ambiguous cases. Risk: data volume blowup from sampling -> cap sampling and use adaptive sampling. Risk: schema churn in span attributes -> register fields with telemetry schema and version with release.

notes_for_oncall: When alerted, open Fault Lens, check top failure class and affected route, sample representative traces (link on panel), follow class-specific runbook. If 'suspect' class is high, escalate to runtime team to review mapping rules. For overload, check autoscaler and node pressure dashboards immediately.
